speakers: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen (host, hedge fund manager; transcribed Neils Krup Larson)
summary: Systematic Investor episode on August 2025 CTA performance, whether CTAs got slower or just more complex, the limits of SG Trend Index as trend beta, and Convex-style long-term compounding with short-term risk mitigation.

coverage.note: intro, sponsor and holiday small talk
Greenland/Fed politics; CTA August performance by sector
oil, speed comparison, gold, rates, carry
trend barometer, index returns, speed vs structure question
correlation-based speed analysis and its limits
speed vs risk management, vol estimation, correlation caveats
66-day half-life, speed definition, trend follower types
trend following objectives and investor expectations
fixed income issuance, loss asymmetry, mean-variance vs compounding, carry analogy
path dependence, solvency, Monte Carlo, insurance
outro: recap repeats earlier idea, next episode plug

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we do see or at least from my vantage point continued strength in um the equity part of the CTA portfolio
claims.claim: In August 2025 CTA gains came from equity trends plus a few commodities (live cattle, gold, silver) while wheat shorts paid on a bumper crop.
claims.direction: long equities, cattle, gold, silver; short wheat
claims.conditions: after a weak H1; vulnerable to policy announcements (copper tariff)
claims.testable: partly - sector attribution can be computed from a trend backtest

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: fixed income in general has been pretty horrible uh for for trend followers because they've been stuck in in large trading ranges
claims.claim: Fixed income was the worst trend-following sector because rates stayed in wide trading ranges and CTAs were split long/short.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: direct attack on another Fed governor uh Lisa Cook um and trying to essentially change the the composition
claims.claim: An attempt to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook could give the administration about five of seven board seats, raising Fed-independence risk.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: oil has kind of just been gyating up and down for for quite a while without too much of real follow through
claims.claim: Oil traded sideways with no follow-through, so energy offered trend followers little.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: broadly speaking the slower the better for the month which seems to be the theme of the the last
claims.claim: Slower trend speeds beat faster ones in recent months and years because V-shaped reversals (April 2025, August 2024) punish fast signals.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: gold for sure. I think gold uh is probably the number one positive contributor year to date out of a universe of like know 80 plus markets
claims.claim: Gold was the top single-market contributor to trend programs in 2025 across an 80+ market universe.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: it's it's it's really kind of going around and whipsing uh with no specific direction
claims.claim: Rates had no trend in 2025, a disappointing year for fixed-income trend contribution.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: Kerry continues to have very very strong month or months or maybe year
claims.claim: Beta-neutralised carry (outside trend following) had one of its best years, so CTAs that add carry, stop-loss or reversion sleeves did better.
claims.testable: yes - add carry sleeve to a trend backtest

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: my own trend barometer actually yesterday finished at 34. So that's still a weak reading.
claims.claim: A trend barometer measuring trendiness over a short lookback read 34 in late August 2025, a weak trend environment consistent with poor CTA returns.
claims.conditions: weak reading means poor trend conditions

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: short-term traders index. It's down one and a quarter% uh and it's now down 6.29%.
claims.claim: In 2025 the short-term traders index was the worst CTA sub-index (-6.29% YTD) versus trend index -7.39% and S&P +11%, so different speeds behaved very differently.
claims.indicator: SG short-term traders index vs SG trend index

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: CTAs have gotten slower over the past decade or so, maybe even more. Um but you question whether that's really a shift in speed or whether that's a shift in structure
claims.claim: Apparent CTA slowing may be a change in structure (added features) rather than a change in signal speed.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: you know if you run this analysis
claims.claim: The usual evidence for CTAs slowing is ex-post: correlate stylised bottom-up fast-to-slow strategies with SG Trend Index on rolling 1-2 year windows and see slower ones correlate more recently.
claims.indicator: rolling correlation of speed-specific trend proxies to SG Trend Index

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: a shift in realized correlations is a necessary but not sufficient condition to infer that the speed has changed
claims.claim: A change in correlation to a benchmark is necessary but not sufficient to infer a change in signal speed.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: It can simply come as a consequence of me introducing stop-loss rules, introducing car signals, introducing reversion signals, amending my program
claims.claim: Adding stop-losses, carry, reversion or value signals, or new markets, shifts correlation to a trend benchmark in the same way a speed change would.
claims.testable: yes - ablation test of added components

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: the fact that the so trend index in itself is a living creature of realized returns of real programs
claims.claim: The SG Trend Index is made of realised returns of real, evolving programs, not a simulation of today's algorithms, so speed-by-correlation analysis on it is questionable.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you can have risk management filters that react much faster and it'll look like uh you have um you know short-term models in there
claims.claim: A long-term trend signal combined with agile risk management can look like a short-term model.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: I think the response is more on the risk management side maybe let's reduce the level of risk we take maybe let's reduce the net or the gross exposure
claims.claim: CTA model research mostly changes risk management (risk level, net/gross exposure, signal diversification) rather than signal speed.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: even changing the way that volatility is estimated or the coverance is estimated or how you penalize some of your exposures might in itself appear exposed as a shift in the speed
claims.claim: Changing volatility or covariance estimation or exposure penalties can show up as an apparent change in speed.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: if I take a correlation of a moment momentum trader to a value investor, I can equally say that it's a contarian
claims.claim: Correlation alone cannot identify a strategy's behaviour: a value investor looks like a contrarian to a momentum trader.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: if we use exponential weighted moving average with the same look back window the story might be slightly different
claims.claim: Conclusions on industry speed depend on market set, signal calculation (EWMA vs simple lookback), so results are fragile.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: know 66 business days of halfife for the last like know 15 years
claims.claim: A paper maximising correlation to SG Trend Index found a best-fit half-life of about 66 business days over 15 years, which is not slow, so the 'CTAs have slowed' story is overstated.
claims.indicator: half-life of EWMA trend signal vs SG Trend Index

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: how can I protect my portfolio, how can be how can I anticipate the signal to noise dropping
claims.claim: CTA research is moving towards protecting the portfolio and anticipating falling signal-to-noise, not choosing a 3, 4 or 5 month speed.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the speed is not constant anyways. I mean we do dynamic select parameters on an ongoing basis
claims.claim: Modern CTAs choose parameters dynamically so speed is not constant, which makes bucketing managers as short/medium/long term misleading.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: different signals in a way um are functional transformations of each other
claims.claim: Different trend signals (sign of past return, EWMA, crossover) are functional transformations of each other, so effort belongs in portfolio construction and risk management rather than signal search (AQR paper).

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you could probably define four or including my extra definition, five types or categories of trend followers
claims.claim: Trend followers split into replicators, core diversifiers, crisis risk offsetters, outlier hunters and pure trend followers, each serving a different investor purpose.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: trend followers or at least the strategy in a broad sense achieves two objectives
claims.claim: Trend following gives defensiveness in prolonged equity or macro drawdowns plus long-term returns, with decorrelation visible over long horizons rather than locally.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: whether you are 10 out of the 12 [L320] months long equities
claims.claim: Longer-term CTAs correlate more with equities long term because they are long in rallies, but they decorrelate around transition points.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: what trend following is used for is that used for a defensive mandate
claims.claim: Whether trend following has worked depends on the investor's purpose (defensive vs absolute return vs inflation hedge); mismatched expectations cause disappointment in years like 2023-2025.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: the more you can dilute trend following programs to make them absolute return, the less defensive by nature you're going to make them
claims.claim: Diluting trend programs to target absolute return makes them less defensive in equity crises.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: Why beta neutral? Because if beta is what you're getting from trend following
claims.claim: Trend following already carries equity beta, so add diversifiers such as beta-neutral carry or reversion rather than more beta.
claims.conditions: when trend is not performing, e.g. 2025

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: It's a snapshot of the 10 biggest managers
claims.claim: The SG Trend Index is the 10 biggest managers, shaped by AUM, survivorship and compromises of running billion-dollar programs, so it is not a pure measure of trend.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: it is the mans that either outperformed so their assets grew by outperformance or they managed to attract capital
claims.claim: Survivorship in the index means it reflects the best surviving managers and sets a higher bar than a plain trend beta.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: we make a supposition here that they average to zero because if they do not average to zero
claims.claim: Calling the manager index 'trend beta' assumes risk-management and design choices net to zero alpha; otherwise it is beta plus or minus alpha.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: a trend benchmark is different to a backtested performance of today's models
claims.claim: A live manager-based trend benchmark differs from a backtest of today's models because manager composition and design evolve through time.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: there are big investors where they are paid bonuses based on their outperformance of these benchmarks
claims.claim: Benchmark definition matters because some investors are paid bonuses on outperformance of trend benchmarks.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: in terms of the daily direction, it seems to align pretty well with what I see from kind of pure trend performance
claims.claim: The SG Trend Indicator (a signal-based, not manager-based index) tracks daily pure-trend performance well.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: I think it would look um very similar to some of the some of the simple bottom up models
claims.claim: A better trend benchmark would be a simple bottom-up trend model as in academic papers, as bank QIS trend indices already do.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: some of the STRs that do not perform you know banks can decide to um to take them out
claims.claim: Third-party aggregated QIS trend indices have survivorship bias since banks drop or replace underperforming strategies.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: people use the 60/40 partly by convention rather than um academic prudence
claims.claim: There is no agreed best allocation benchmark, similar to 60/40 being used by convention.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: if you want to build your portfolio um to have the highest long-term uh return
claims.claim: Following Dave Dredge (Convex): portfolios built to look safe and near long-term average load up on correlated strategies that fall together; maximising long-term compounding requires different construction.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you kind of have to build the car to have the best best brakes
claims.claim: Race-car analogy: best 'brakes' (long volatility, trend following) let a portfolio run faster over the long run.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it actually allows you to own more equities. Um so you could have an 80/20 portfolio
claims.claim: Including crisis-protective strategies allows higher equity allocation (e.g. 80/20 instead of 60/40).
claims.direction: more equities when hedged with trend/long vol

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the issuance of fixed income products will just continue to grow
claims.claim: Fiscal expansion means rising bond issuance, so portfolios will hold more fixed income, which is not a safe source of long-term real compounding.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: losing 10% would require you an 11% gain to go back to flat
claims.claim: Losses compound asymmetrically (10% loss needs about 11% to recover), so short-term losses reduce long-term compounding.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: the expected returns is now a long-term capital appreciation whereas the risk that we want to minimize becomes more of a short-term risk mitigation
claims.claim: Unlike single-period mean-variance, a compounding investor targets long-horizon return while minimising short-horizon risk.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: how a a a carry harvesting investor would perform or would operate
claims.claim: Carry harvesting resembles buying rental property: the yield is earned but spot-price drops can erase it, so short-term spot moves need controlling.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: the short-term drop doesn't have an impact on the day but does have an impact on how the acrual or the accumulation of wealth will play out
claims.claim: Short-term drawdowns matter for how wealth accumulates over years, not just terminal wealth.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: you actually want to make sure that you can pay your pensions on an annual basis
claims.claim: Pension and income funds have annual solvency checkpoints, making short-term risk mitigation a requirement alongside long-term growth.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: the simulated compounded return would be substantially skewed to the to the right
claims.claim: Monte Carlo sampling of 12-52 period sequences shows strategies with short-term downside mitigation (long vol, trend) have similar average arithmetic returns but a compounded return distribution shifted right.

claims.speaker: Nick Bolters
claims.quote: we pay insurance. Like in reality, insurance is a negative expected return investment
claims.claim: Long volatility or trend exposure should be judged in portfolio context, like insurance with negative standalone expected return that pays when needed.
